facts.value: Aman Group is expanding beyond luxury hospitality with ATMA, a new brand built around performance, wellness, and sport. The first destination, ATMA Miami, will include a hotel, branded residences, and a private members club. Centered around a 120K-sq-ft spa and wellness center, it features fitness facilities, racket courts, mobility and conditioning labs, a medical wellness center, and dedicated recovery spaces. Tennis champion and Aman global partner Novak Djokovic will lead the brand’s longevity, nutrition, racquet sports, and wellness programming, drawing on his experience as an elite athlete.

topic: Men Join the Pilates Boom, On’s Premium Play Pays Off, Seed Oil-Free Snacks Hit $1B

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Men Join the Pilates Boom, On’s Premium Play Pays Off, Seed Oil-Free Snacks Hit $1B Men now make up roughly a third of Pilates participants, signaling a shift in the once female-dominated workout. The shift is changing the market for studios. Brands like Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are benefiting from more co-ed demand as studios look to reach both men and women with the same programming and messaging. The Swiss sportswear brand reported Q3 sales of about $1.1B, up 17.2% YoY. The strategy is working so far: On expects full-year sales growth in the 20% range and is targeting $7B in annual revenue by 2029. Rather than compete on discounts, it’s scaling premium products, athlete partnerships, and a broader lifestyle offering while larger rivals struggle. Americans spent more than $1B on products labeled seed oil-free over the past year, up more than 72% from the year before, according to NielsenIQ data. For food brands, the seed oil debate is becoming a commercial force. But reformulating around a health trend also raises questions about cost, ingredient quality, and how much consumers are willing to spend on clean label options.

topic: HFA Outlines Three-Year Strategic Direction, Names Greta Wagner President and CEO

facts.label: Story
facts.value: HFA Outlines Three-Year Strategic Direction, Names Greta Wagner President and CEO

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The association’s three-year strategy focuses on delivering greater member value, strengthening advocacy, and expanding the health and fitness industry’s influence. Greta Wagner has been named president and CEO at the Health & Fitness Association after serving six months in an interim role. She will lead the implementation of a new three-year strategy plan. The Health & Fitness Association (HFA) has developed a three-year strategic plan designed to strengthen the association, deliver greater value to members, and elevate the health and fitness industry’s influence. Leading that initiative is Greta Wagner, who was named HFA’s permanent president and CEO after six months in the interim role. The announcements were made November 12 at Beyond Activ Americas in Dallas. Working with the HFA Board of Directors, leadership team, and industry stakeholders, Wagner led the development of a plan to make HFA a more relevant, influential, and valuable resource for its members. “Greta has challenged us to think differently about how we serve our members, where we focus our resources, and how we measure success,” said Luke Carlson, chair of the HFA Board of Directors. “The result is a strategy grounded in the needs of our industry, supported by an aligned leadership team, and focused on meaningful results.
